name: Zignify
summary: End-to-end ownership of the web stack — plus an AI content engine and programmatic SEO pages built on top of WordPress.
client: Zignify — global product sourcing, quality control and logistics
role: Web development, automation & SEO — sole technical owner
overview: Zignify helps companies source products globally, handling quality control, logistics and shipping. I own their web stack end to end: domains, DNS, server administration and security, and full-stack WordPress development. On top of that foundation I build the systems that let a small marketing operation publish and rank at a scale that would normally need a much larger team.
challenge: A sourcing business competes on visibility for a very wide range of product and market searches. Writing, formatting and publishing every article by hand doesn't scale, and hand-built landing pages drift out of date. The site needed to stay technically sound while content and pages were produced continuously — and the marketing side needed CRM and email automation that actually connected to the website.

approach.title: Own the foundation
approach.description: Took over domains, DNS, server administration and security so that every later automation runs on infrastructure I control and can troubleshoot directly.

approach.title: Turn tasks into published content
approach.description: Built a content engine where a ClickUp task becomes the brief: the system generates an SEO-ready article with AI assistance and publishes it to WordPress automatically, with no copy-paste step in between.

approach.title: Generate pages from data
approach.description: Developed programmatic SEO page systems that create and update large sets of landing pages from structured data, so pages are produced consistently and refreshed when the data changes.

approach.title: Keep it indexable
approach.description: Backed the volume with technical SEO — indexing control, schema markup and Core Web Vitals — so automated output stays crawlable and fast.

approach.title: Connect marketing
approach.description: Set up and connected GoHighLevel (CRM, funnels, workflows) and Klaviyo (email flows, segmentation) to the web stack.

delivered: Domain, DNS, server administration and security — end to end
ClickUp → AI → WordPress content automation engine
Programmatic SEO landing-page systems driven by structured data
Technical SEO: indexing, schema, Core Web Vitals

name: IDSA
summary: Drupal to WordPress migration for the Infectious Diseases Society of America, with an ACF content architecture across 100+ pages.
client: Infectious Diseases Society of America — medical association
engagement: via newtarget, inc. (Washington, DC) — part of the development team
overview: IDSA is a medical association representing physicians, scientists and other healthcare professionals who specialise in infectious diseases. Its website is a large, content-heavy resource for members and the public. Working on the newtarget team, I took part in moving the site from Drupal to WordPress and in designing the content structure it now runs on.
challenge: Migrating a large, established site between CMSs is never a straight copy. Drupal and WordPress model content differently, so structured content has to be re-mapped rather than pasted; editors need a system they can manage without breaking layouts; and 100+ pages have to arrive intact. The new architecture had to make the site easier to maintain, not just different.

approach.title: Model the content first
approach.description: Defined an ACF-based content architecture — structured fields and reusable layouts instead of free-form pages — so content is consistent across the site and editors work with clear inputs.

approach.title: Build the templates on that model
approach.description: Implemented custom WordPress templates that render the structured content, keeping presentation and data separate.

approach.title: Migrate and verify
approach.description: Moved 100+ pages from Drupal into the new structure and checked them against the source.

approach.title: Ship through the pipeline
approach.description: Supported deployment through newtarget's DevOps setup — CI/CD pipelines, deployments and security updates.

outcome: 100+ pages migrated from Drupal to WordPress
